items.title: The quaternion rotation map $\rho$: conjugation on the imaginary quaternions, the unit sphere $S^3$, and quaternion lifts
items.statement:
Let $\mathbb H$ be the quaternion algebra with its product, conjugation $x\mapsto\bar x$, real-valued norm $N:\mathbb H\to\mathbb R$, and real embedding $r\mapsto\hat r=(r,0,0,0)$, in the notation of [[def-quaternions]]. Thus $x=x_0+x_1i+x_2j+x_3k$ with the multiplication formula of [[def-quaternions]], and

$$N(x)=x_0^2+x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2,\qquad \widehat{N(x)}=x\bar x=\bar x x.$$

In particular, $N(x)>0$ for $x\ne0$, and the imported division-ring theorem gives the typed inverse formula $x^{-1}=\widehat{N(x)^{-1}}\,\bar x$ ([[thm-quaternions-form-a-division-ring]]). Under the identification of $\mathbb H$ with $\mathbb R^4$ by the coordinates $x_0,\dots,x_3$ one has $N(x)=\|x\|_2^2$ for the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]].

**Imaginary quaternions and the vector identification.** Put

$$\operatorname{Im}\mathbb H:=\{x\in\mathbb H:\bar x=-x\}=\mathbb Ri\oplus\mathbb Rj\oplus\mathbb Rk,\qquad \varphi:\mathbb R^3\to\operatorname{Im}\mathbb H,\quad \varphi(v_1,v_2,v_3):=v_1i+v_2j+v_3k .$$

Then $\varphi$ is a linear isomorphism with $N(\varphi(v))=\|v\|_2^2$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^3$. Throughout the collection, $\varphi$ translates between vectors of $\mathbb R^3$ (their inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_2$, norm $\|\cdot\|_2$ and cross product) and imaginary quaternions inside quaternion products.

**The unit sphere.** Define

$$S^3:=\{q\in\mathbb H:N(q)=1\},$$

the unit sphere of $\mathbb H\cong\mathbb R^4$. The identification of $S^3$ with $SU(2)$ is the one of the published covering example `ex-su-two-to-so-three-as-a-covering-homomorphism`, which is also the source of the covering statement recorded in the second remark below; that example is linked from the page summary of this pair.

**Conjugation and the rotation map.** For $q\in\mathbb H$ with $q\ne0$ let $c_q:\mathbb H\to\mathbb H$ be

$$c_q(x):=qxq^{-1}=qx\,\widehat{N(q)^{-1}}\,\bar q,$$

where the real scalar is embedded by $r\mapsto\hat r$, and define

$$\rho(q):=c_q|_{\operatorname{Im}\mathbb H}:\operatorname{Im}\mathbb H\longrightarrow\operatorname{Im}\mathbb H .$$

Both the $\mathbb R$-linear map $\rho(q)$ and its matrix in the ordered basis $(i,j,k)$ of $\operatorname{Im}\mathbb H$ are written $\rho(q)$; the equality $\rho(q)\in SO(3)$ for $q\in S^3$ is part of the cited covering statement, and the matrix is the one meant whenever $\rho(q)$ is composed with the identifications above. The map $\rho$ itself is never linear in $q$ and no such structure is used.

**Quaternion lifts.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval and let $R:I\to SO(3)$ be a map, with $SO(3)$ as in [[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]]. A **quaternion lift** of $R$ is a map $q:I\to S^3$ with $\rho(q(t))=R(t)$ for every $t\in I$.

references.title: P. Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I (Fall 2020), Exercise 3.9 (conjugation action of SU(2) on traceless Hermitian matrices and the covering SU(2) -> SO(3)), printed page 26, and Proposition 6.7 (unit quaternions are isomorphic to SU(2)), printed page 40

A. W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, Digital Second Edition (2023), Introduction, Problems 7-9 (construction of a smooth homomorphism SU(2) -> SO(3) with kernel {+I,-I}), printed pages 20-21, and Section I.8 (the quaternion division algebra, conjugation, Re xy = Re yx), printed pages 56-58

J. Sola, Quaternion kinematics for the error-state Kalman filter (arXiv:1711.02508), Section 2.3 (the rotation group and the rotation matrix: R^T R = I, det R = 1, the group SO(3)), printed pages 14-19, and Section 2.4.6 (the double cover of SO(3); R{-q} = R{q}), printed page 24

items.title: The product rule for quaternion and matrix curves, multiplicativity of the quaternion norm, and the conjugation formula $q\,\varphi(v)\,\bar q=\varphi\bigl((a^{2}-\|u\|^{2})v+2\langle u,v\rangle u+2a\,(u\times v)\bigr)$
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nondegenerate open interval, let $\mathbb H$ be the quaternions, and let $\varphi:\mathbb R^3\to\operatorname{Im}\mathbb H$ be the identification of [[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]].

1. **Product form and product rule.** For $p=s+\varphi(u)$ and $q=t+\varphi(w)$ with $s,t\in\mathbb R$ and $u,w\in\mathbb R^3$ one has $pq=\bigl(st-\langle u,w\rangle_2\bigr)+\varphi\bigl(sw+tu+u\times w\bigr)$. If moreover $p,q:I\to\mathbb H$ are of class $C^1$ (componentwise, [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), then $pq:I\to\mathbb H$ is $C^1$ and $(pq)'=p'q+pq'$. Likewise, if $A,B:I\to M_3(\mathbb R)$ are of class $C^1$, then $AB$ is $C^1$ and $(AB)'=A'B+AB'$.
2. **Conjugation and norm.** For all $p,q\in\mathbb H$ one has $\overline{pq}=\bar q\,\bar p$ and $N(pq)=N(p)N(q)$, and $\operatorname{Re}(p\bar q)=\langle p,q\rangle_2$ for $\operatorname{Re}(x):=x_0$ and the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. For a $C^1$ curve $q:I\to\mathbb H$, the curves $\bar q$ and $N\circ q$ are $C^1$ with $\overline{q}'=\overline{q'}$ and

$$(N\circ q)'=2\operatorname{Re}(q'\bar q)=2\langle q',q\rangle_2 .$$

3. **Conjugation formula.** If $q=a+\varphi(u)$ with $a\in\mathbb R$ and $u\in\mathbb R^3$, and $v\in\mathbb R^3$, then

$$q\,\varphi(v)\,\bar q=\varphi\Bigl((a^2-\|u\|_2^2)\,v+2\langle u,v\rangle_2\,u+2a\,(u\times v)\Bigr);$$

in particular $q\,\varphi(v)\,\bar q$ is imaginary for every $q\in\mathbb H$, that is, its real part is $0$.
4. **Axis-angle form.** If $N(q)=1$ and $q=\cos(\theta/2)+\varphi(\hat n)\sin(\theta/2)$ with $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and $\hat n\in\mathbb R^3$, $\|\hat n\|_2=1$, then for every $v\in\mathbb R^3$

$$\rho(q)\bigl(\varphi(v)\bigr)=\varphi\Bigl(\cos\theta\,v+(1-\cos\theta)\langle \hat n,v\rangle_2\,\hat n+\sin\theta\,(\hat n\times v)\Bigr).$$

references.title: J. Sola, Quaternion kinematics for the error-state Kalman filter (arXiv:1711.02508), Section 1.2 (quaternion product, conjugate, norm and inverse: equations (24)-(30)), printed page 8, and Section 2.5 (the quaternion-to-rotation-matrix formula R = (q_w^2 - q_v^T q_v) I + 2 q_v q_v^T + 2 q_w [q_v]_x, equation (117)), printed page 25
P. Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I (Fall 2020), Section 6.2 (quaternions: conjugate, norm, anti-automorphism and multiplicativity |q_1 q_2| = |q_1||q_2|), printed pages 39-40
A. W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, Digital Second Edition (2023), Introduction, Section I.8 (quaternion algebra: x xbar = |x|^2, Re xy = Re yx), printed pages 56-58

items.title: The body angular velocity of a $C^1$ rotation path: $\Omega=R^{\mathsf T}R'$ is skew, $\Omega z=\omega\times z$ determines a unique continuous $\omega$, and $R'=R\Omega$
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nondegenerate open interval, let $SO(3)$ be as in [[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]], and let $R:I\to SO(3)$ be of class $C^1$, that is, all nine entries of $R$ have continuous first derivatives; write $R'(t)$ for the entrywise derivative and put

$$\Omega(t):=R(t)^{\mathsf T}R'(t)\in M_3(\mathbb R)$$

for the product of the transpose of $R(t)$ with $R'(t)$ ([[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]], [[def-matrix-space]]). Then:

1. $\Omega(t)$ is skew-symmetric for every $t\in I$, that is $\Omega(t)^{\mathsf T}=-\Omega(t)$.
2. There is exactly one map $\omega:I\to\mathbb R^3$ with

$$R(t)^{\mathsf T}R'(t)\,z=\omega(t)\times z\qquad(z\in\mathbb R^3,\ t\in I),$$

namely $\omega(t)=\bigl(-\Omega_{23}(t),\ \Omega_{13}(t),\ -\Omega_{12}(t)\bigr)$, and this $\omega$ is continuous. It is called the **body angular velocity** of $R$.
3. For every $t\in I$, writing $\Omega_{\omega(t)}$ for the matrix $z\mapsto\omega(t)\times z$, one has $R'(t)=R(t)\,\Omega_{\omega(t)}$.

references.title: J. Sola, Quaternion kinematics for the error-state Kalman filter (arXiv:1711.02508), Section 2.3.1 (differentiating R^T R: R^T Rdot is skew-symmetric, equations (63)-(66)), printed pages 16-18, and Section 4.5 ((200): Rdot = R [omega_L]_x for body-referenced angular rates), printed pages 45-46

N. Trawny and S. I. Roumeliotis, Indirect Kalman Filter for 3D Attitude Estimation (University of Minnesota, TR-2005-002), Section 1.2 (quaternion multiplication, inverse and conjugate quaternion, equations (21)-(23)), printed pages 3-4, and Section 1.5 (quaternion time derivative for a moving frame, equations (80)-(89)), printed pages 9-10

A. W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, Digital Second Edition (2023), Introduction, Section 1 (the linear Lie algebra so(3) consists of the skew-symmetric real 3-by-3 matrices), printed pages 5-6

items.title: The quaternion lift of a prescribed continuous angular velocity: $q'=\tfrac12 q\,\varphi(\omega(t))$ keeps $S^3$ invariant, its rotation path has body angular velocity $\omega$, and the initial value problem has a unique solution on the whole interval
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nondegenerate open interval, let $\omega:I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous, and consider on the open time-state domain $D:=I\times\mathbb H\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb H$ the initial value problem

$$q'(t)=\tfrac12\,q(t)\,\varphi\bigl(\omega(t)\bigr),\qquad q(t_0)=q_0,$$

read as the first-order system of [[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]] with time-state domain $D$, state space $\mathbb H$, and right-hand side $F:D\to\mathbb H$, $F(t,q)=\tfrac12q\,\varphi(\omega(t))$, where $\varphi$, $S^3$ and $\rho$ are those of [[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]].

1. If $q:I\to\mathbb H$ is a $C^1$ solution of $q'=\tfrac12q\,\varphi(\omega(t))$, then $N\circ q$ is constant on $I$; if $q(t_0)\in S^3$ for one $t_0\in I$, then $q(I)\subseteq S^3$ and the curve

$$R:=\rho\circ q:I\longrightarrow SO(3),\qquad R(t):=\rho(q(t)),$$

is of class $C^1$ with $R'(t)=R(t)\,\Omega_{\omega(t)}$ for every $t\in I$; consequently $\omega$ is the body angular velocity of $R$ in the sense of [[lem-cm-body-angular-velocity-of-a-rotation-path]].
2. For every $t_0\in I$ and $q_0\in S^3$ the problem has exactly one maximal solution, and its domain is all of $I$; that is, there is exactly one $C^1$ curve $q:I\to S^3$ with $q(t_0)=q_0$ and $q'=\tfrac12q\,\varphi(\omega(t))$ on $I$, and clause 1 applies to it.

references.title: J. Sola, Quaternion kinematics for the error-state Kalman filter (arXiv:1711.02508), Section 2.4.1 ((90)-(93): q* qdot is a pure quaternion and qdot = q (x) Omega) and Section 2.4.2 ((97)-(99): omega = 2 Omega, qdot = (1/2) q (x) omega, q = e^{omega t/2}), printed pages 20-22

N. Trawny and S. I. Roumeliotis, Indirect Kalman Filter for 3D Attitude Estimation (University of Minnesota, TR-2005-002), Section 1.5 (quaternion time derivative of a moving frame, equations (80)-(89)), printed pages 9-10

G. Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems (AMS Graduate Studies in Mathematics 140, online edition), Section 2.1 (fixed point theorems and the contraction principle), Section 2.2 (the basic existence and uniqueness result, Theorem 2.2), Section 2.3 (some extensions), Section 2.6 (extensibility of solutions: Theorem 2.13 and Corollary 2.15), printed pages 33-41 and 50-53

items.title: Angular-velocity reconstruction from a unit-quaternion path: for $C^1$ $q:I\to S^3$ the body angular velocity of $\rho\circ q$ is $\omega=2\varphi^{-1}(q^{-1}q')$
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nondegenerate open interval, let $q:I\to S^3$ be of class $C^1$, and let

$$R:I\longrightarrow SO(3),\qquad R(t):=\rho(q(t)),$$

be the associated rotation path, the matrix being taken in the basis $(i,j,k)$ of $\operatorname{Im}\mathbb H$ ([[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]]). Then:

1. $q(t)^{-1}q'(t)=\bar q(t)q'(t)$ has real part $0$ for every $t\in I$, so it lies in $\operatorname{Im}\mathbb H$ and there is a unique vector $\omega(t)\in\mathbb R^3$ with

$$q(t)^{-1}q'(t)=\tfrac12\,\varphi\bigl(\omega(t)\bigr),$$

namely $\omega(t)=2\varphi^{-1}\bigl(q(t)^{-1}q'(t)\bigr)$, where $\varphi^{-1}:\operatorname{Im}\mathbb H\to\mathbb R^3$ is the inverse of the isomorphism in [[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]]; $t\mapsto\omega(t)$ is continuous.
2. The curve $q$ solves $q'(t)=\tfrac12q(t)\,\varphi(\omega(t))$ on $I$, the matrix curve $R$ is of class $C^1$, and $R'(t)=R(t)\,\Omega_{\omega(t)}$ for every $t\in I$, where $\Omega_{\omega(t)}$ is the matrix $z\mapsto\omega(t)\times z$.
3. Consequently $\omega$ is the body angular velocity of $R$ in the sense of [[lem-cm-body-angular-velocity-of-a-rotation-path]]: $R$ is a $C^1$ rotation path whose body angular velocity is $\omega$.

references.title: J. Sola, Quaternion kinematics for the error-state Kalman filter (arXiv:1711.02508), Section 2.4.1, equation (91)-(92): q* (x) qdot is a pure quaternion, q* (x) qdot = Omega; Section 2.4.2, equation (99): omega = 2 Omega and qdot = (1/2) q (x) omega

N. Trawny and S. I. Roumeliotis, Indirect Kalman Filter for 3D Attitude Estimation (University of Minnesota, TR-2005-002), Section 1.5, equations (80)-(89): qdot = (1/2) [omega;0] (x) q for a unit quaternion and the local (body) angular rate omega

items.title: Existence, uniqueness and sign ambiguity of the quaternion lift of a $C^1$ rotation path
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nondegenerate open interval, let $R:I\to SO(3)$ be of class $C^1$ ([[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]]) with body angular velocity $\omega_R$ in the sense of [[lem-cm-body-angular-velocity-of-a-rotation-path]], let $t_0\in I$, and let $q_0\in S^3$ satisfy $\rho(q_0)=R(t_0)$, with $\rho$ and $S^3$ as in [[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]]. Then:

1. There is exactly one $C^1$ quaternion lift $q:I\to S^3$ of $R$ with $q(t_0)=q_0$, namely the unique solution on $I$ of the initial value problem

$$q'(t)=\tfrac12\,q(t)\,\varphi\bigl(\omega_R(t)\bigr),\qquad q(t_0)=q_0 .$$

2. Every $C^1$ lift $\tilde q:I\to S^3$ of $R$ satisfies $\tilde q=q$ or $\tilde q=-q$; in particular $-q$ is the lift with initial value $-q_0$, and $\rho\circ q=\rho\circ(-q)=R$.

references.title: J. Sola, Quaternion kinematics for the error-state Kalman filter (arXiv:1711.02508), Section 2.4.2 (q = e^{omega t/2} solves qdot = (1/2) q (x) omega), printed pages 21-22, and Section 2.4.6 (the double cover: q and -q encode the same rotation), printed page 24

N. Trawny and S. I. Roumeliotis, Indirect Kalman Filter for 3D Attitude Estimation (University of Minnesota, TR-2005-002), Section 1.1 (a quaternion and its negative describe the same rotation) printed page 2, and Section 1.5 (quaternion time derivative), printed pages 9-10
A. W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, Digital Second Edition (2023), Introduction, Problems 7-9 (kernel {+I,-I} of the homomorphism SU(2) -> SO(3)), printed pages 20-21

items.title: Scope of the quaternion lift: the global sign ambiguity, closed loops, and the absence of a physical spin claim
items.statement:
The following qualifications are part of what the preceding items do and do not claim.

1. **Two lifts and one rotation.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nondegenerate open interval and let $R:I\to SO(3)$ be of class $C^1$. By [[thm-cm-quaternion-lift-exists-and-is-unique]], $R$ has exactly two $C^1$ quaternion lifts, namely $q$ and $-q$ for any one lift $q$, both solve $q'=\tfrac12q\,\varphi(\omega_R(t))$ for the same body angular velocity $\omega_R$, and $\rho(q)=\rho(-q)=R$. By the scaling recorded in [[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]], $\rho(\hat\lambda q)=\rho(q)$ for every nonzero real $\lambda$, so a rotation is represented by the antipodal pair $\pm q$ of unit quaternions and by no other data of the quaternion itself.

2. **No globally continuous sign choice.** The sign of a lift is not determined by $R$, and the two signs cannot always be glued continuously along closed motion. The companion examples page exhibits a loop $R:[0,1]\to SO(3)$, continuous on $[0,1]$ and $C^1$ on $(0,1)$, with $R(0)=R(1)=I_3$, whose explicit lift from $1$ ends at $-1$. By uniqueness on the interior and continuity at the endpoints, this loop admits no closed lift through $1$ with that regularity; the explicit counterexample is linked in the Remarks below. In this sense the sign ambiguity is intrinsic and not an artifact of the formula $\rho(q)(x)=qxq^{-1}$.

3. **No physical claim.** Every statement on this page concerns curves into $S^3$ and into the matrix group $SO(3)$ and the differential equation $q'=\tfrac12q\,\varphi(\omega(t))$. No quantum-mechanical spin, relativistic, or half-integer-angular-momentum interpretation is asserted, no measurement is reported, and no empirical precision is claimed anywhere.

references.title: J. Sola, Quaternion kinematics for the error-state Kalman filter (arXiv:1711.02508), Section 2.4.6 (the double cover of SO(3): a full 2pi turn of the rotation corresponds to a half turn of the quaternion vector, so q and -q encode the same rotation), printed page 24
P. Etingof, MIT 18.745 Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I (Fall 2020), Exercise 3.9(ii) (SU(2) -> SO(3) is a universal covering; pi_1(SO(3)) = Z/2; the Dirac belt trick), printed page 26

items.title: Constant angular velocity: the lift $q(t)=\cos(\omega_0t/2)+\varphi(\hat n)\sin(\omega_0t/2)$ is the rotation about $\hat n$ through $\omega_0t$, and a full turn lifts to the antipode
items.statement:
For a curve on a closed interval $[0,T]$, this item uses "$C^1$ on $[0,T]$" to mean continuous on $[0,T]$ and $C^1$ on $(0,T)$; no endpoint derivatives are required.

Fix $\omega_0\in\mathbb R$ and a unit vector $\hat n\in\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), put $\omega:=\omega_0\hat n$, and consider

$$q:\mathbb R\longrightarrow S^3,\qquad q(t):=\cos(\omega_0t/2)+\varphi(\hat n)\sin(\omega_0t/2),$$

with $\varphi$ and $S^3$ as in [[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]]. Then:

1. $q$ is of class $C^1$ with $q(0)=1$, and $q$ solves the lift equation $q'(t)=\tfrac12q(t)\,\varphi(\omega)$ on $\mathbb R$.
2. The curve $R:=\rho\circ q:\mathbb R\to SO(3)$ is of class $C^1$ with $R'(t)=R(t)\,\Omega_\omega$ for all $t$; that is, $\omega$ is the constant body angular velocity of $R$. Explicitly, $R(t)$ is the rotation about $\hat n$ through the angle $\omega_0t$:

$$R(t)\,\varphi(v)=\varphi\Bigl(\cos(\omega_0t)\,v+\bigl(1-\cos(\omega_0t)\bigr)\langle \hat n,v\rangle_2\,\hat n+\sin(\omega_0t)\,(\hat n\times v)\Bigr)\qquad(v\in\mathbb R^3).$$

3. If $\omega_0\ne0$, set $T:=2\pi/|\omega_0|>0$. Then $R(0)=R(T)=I_3$ while $q(T)=-1\ne q(0)$, and the closed loop $t\mapsto R(t)$ on $[0,T]$ has no closed lift through $1$ with the closed-interval regularity just defined.

references.title: J. Sola, Quaternion kinematics for the error-state Kalman filter (arXiv:1711.02508), Section 2.4.2 (Exp(phi u) = cos(phi/2) + u sin(phi/2); q = e^{omega t/2} for constant omega), printed pages 21-22, and Section 2.4.6 (a full 2pi rotation corresponds to q -> -q), printed page 24

N. Trawny and S. I. Roumeliotis, Indirect Kalman Filter for 3D Attitude Estimation (University of Minnesota, TR-2005-002), Section 1.1 (quaternion of rotation q = [k sin(theta/2); cos(theta/2)], equation (4), and the statement that q and -q describe the same rotation), printed page 2

items.title: A time-varying rate about a fixed axis: $q(t)=q_0\bigl(\cos((\theta(t)-\theta(0))/2)+\varphi(\hat n)\sin((\theta(t)-\theta(0))/2)\bigr)$ solves the lift equation with $\omega(t)=\theta'(t)\hat n$
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nondegenerate open interval with $0\in I$, let $\theta:I\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^1$, let $\hat n\in\mathbb R^3$ be a unit vector, let $q_0\in S^3$, and define the normalized phase $\alpha(t):=\theta(t)-\theta(0)$ and

$$e(t):=\cos\bigl(\alpha(t)/2\bigr)+\varphi(\hat n)\sin\bigl(\alpha(t)/2\bigr),\qquad q(t):=q_0\,e(t),$$

with $\varphi,S^3,\rho$ as in [[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]]. Then:

1. $e$ and $q$ are of class $C^1$, they take values in $S^3$, and $q(0)=q_0$.
2. The curve $q$ solves $q'(t)=\tfrac12q(t)\,\varphi(\omega(t))$ with $\omega(t):=\theta'(t)\hat n$, on all of $I$.
3. Consequently $R:=\rho\circ q$ is a $C^1$ rotation path whose body angular velocity is $\omega(t)=\theta'(t)\hat n$, and $R(t)=\rho(q_0)\rho(e(t))$, where $\rho(e(t))$ is the rotation about $\hat n$ through the angle $\alpha(t)=\theta(t)-\theta(0)$.

references.title: J. Sola, Quaternion kinematics for the error-state Kalman filter (arXiv:1711.02508), Section 2.4.2 (q = e^{omega t/2}; Exp(phi u) = cos(phi/2) + u sin(phi/2)) and Section 2.4.3 (quaternion and rotation vector), printed pages 21-22

N. Trawny and S. I. Roumeliotis, Indirect Kalman Filter for 3D Attitude Estimation (University of Minnesota, TR-2005-002), Section 1.1 (axis-angle construction of the quaternion of rotation, equation (4)), printed page 2, and Section 1.4 (relationship between quaternion and rotation matrix; small-rotation approximation), printed pages 6-8

items.title: A non-axis-constant check of the reconstruction formula: for $q=(\cos\tfrac t2+\varphi(e_1)\sin\tfrac t2)(\cos\tfrac t2+\varphi(e_2)\sin\tfrac t2)$ one gets $\omega(t)=(\cos t,1,\sin t)$
items.statement:
On $I=\mathbb R$ define

$$u(t):=\cos(t/2)+\varphi(e_1)\sin(t/2),\qquad v(t):=\cos(t/2)+\varphi(e_2)\sin(t/2),\qquad q(t):=u(t)\,v(t),$$

where $e_1,e_2,e_3$ is the standard basis of $\mathbb R^3$, $\varphi$ is the identification of [[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]], and the product is the quaternion product. Then:

1. $q:\mathbb R\to S^3$ is of class $C^1$.
2. $\bar uu'=\tfrac12\varphi(e_1)$ and $\bar vv'=\tfrac12\varphi(e_2)$, and

$$q(t)^{-1}q'(t)=\bar v(t)\bigl(\bar u(t)u'(t)\bigr)v(t)+\bar v(t)v'(t)=\tfrac12\,\varphi\bigl(\cos t\,e_1+e_2+\sin t\,e_3\bigr).$$

3. Consequently $R=\rho\circ q$ is a $C^1$ rotation path whose body angular velocity is $\omega(t)=\cos t\,e_1+e_2+\sin t\,e_3$, that is, $\omega(t)=(\cos t,1,\sin t)$ in coordinates; this $\omega$ is neither constant nor along a fixed axis.

references.title: J. Sola, Quaternion kinematics for the error-state Kalman filter (arXiv:1711.02508), Section 2.4.1-2.4.2 (q* qdot pure; omega = 2 Omega) and Section 2.6 (quaternion composition q_AC = q_AB (x) q_BC), printed pages 20-22 and 26-27

N. Trawny and S. I. Roumeliotis, Indirect Kalman Filter for 3D Attitude Estimation (University of Minnesota, TR-2005-002), Section 1.2 (quaternion multiplication and composition), printed pages 2-4, and Section 1.5 (quaternion time derivative), printed pages 9-10

items.title: Finite checks of the cover: the half-turn rotations $\rho(\pm i),\rho(\pm j),\rho(\pm k)$, the identity $\rho(i)\rho(j)=\rho(ij)$, and the exact preimages of $\rho(k)$
items.statement:
Let $e_1,e_2,e_3$ be the standard basis of $\mathbb R^3$ and identify $\mathbb R^3$ with $\operatorname{Im}\mathbb H$ through $\varphi$ as in [[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]]; matrices of linear maps are taken in the ordered basis $(i,j,k)$. Then:

1. $\rho(1)$ is the identity matrix and $\rho(-1)=\rho(1)$; moreover, if $q\in S^3$ satisfies $\rho(q)=I_3$, then $q=\pm1$.
2. $\rho(i),\rho(j),\rho(k)$ are the half-turns about the coordinate axes,

$$\rho(i)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&-1&0\\0&0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad \rho(j)=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad \rho(k)=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0&0\\0&-1&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix},$$

and $\rho(i)\rho(j)=\rho(k)=\rho(ij)$: the homomorphism identity is verified on the generating pair $i,j$ by finite matrix multiplication.
3. The exact preimages of $\rho(k)$ in $S^3$ are $\pm k$: $\rho(\pm k)=\rho(k)$, and every $q\in S^3$ with $\rho(q)=\rho(k)$ satisfies $q=\pm k$.

items.title: A closed rotation loop with no closed lift: the full turn about an axis lifts from $1$ to $-1$
items.statement:
In this item, a curve on $[0,1]$ is called $C^1$ when it is continuous on $[0,1]$ and its restriction to $(0,1)$ is $C^1$; no endpoint derivatives are required.

For every closed $C^1$ curve $R:[0,1]\to SO(3)$ with $R(0)=R(1)=I_3$ and every $q_0\in S^3$ with $\rho(q_0)=I_3$, there exists a $C^1$ lift $q:[0,1]\to S^3$ of $R$ with $q(0)=q(1)=q_0$.
